arxiv-2104-13043.title: LAST at CMCL 2021 Shared Task: Predicting Gaze Data During Reading with a Gradient Boosting Decision Tree Approach
arxiv-2104-13043.creator: Yves Bestgen
arxiv-2104-13043.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yves Bestgen. A LightGBM model fed with target word lexical characteristics and features obtained from word frequency lists, psychometric data and bigram association measures has been optimized for the 2021 CMCL Shared Task on Eye-Tracking Data Prediction. It obtained the best performance of all teams on two of the five eye-tracking measures to predict, allowing it to rank first on the official challenge criterion and to outperform all deep-learning based systems participating in the challenge.

arxiv-2106-03372.title: A consistent nonparametric test of the effect of dementia duration on mortality
arxiv-2106-03372.creator: L Radloff, R Weißbach, C Reinke, G Doblhammer
arxiv-2106-03372.description: Abstract A continuous-time multi-state history is semi-Markovian, if an intensity to migrate from one state into another, depends on the duration in the first state. Such duration can be formalised as covariate, entering the intensity process of the transition counts. We derive the integrated intensity process, prove its predictability and the martingale property of the residual.

arxiv-2107-05296.title: Separating LREC from LFP Thanks: Research funded in part by EPSRC grant EP/S03238X/1.
arxiv-2107-05296.creator: Anuj Dawar, Felipe Ferreira Santos
arxiv-2107-05296.description: Abstract LREC = \textsf{LREC}_{=} is an extension of first-order logic with a logarithmic recursion operator. It was introduced by Grohe et al. and shown to capture the complexity class L \mathrm{L} over trees and interval graphs. It does not capture L \mathrm{L} in general as it is contained in FPC —fixed-point logic with counting.

arxiv-2205-02461.title: Fracture of silicate glasses: Micro-cavities and correlations between atomic-level properties
arxiv-2205-02461.creator: Zhen Zhang, Simona Ispas, Walter Kob
arxiv-2205-02461.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Zhen Zhang, Simona Ispas, Walter Kob. We use large-scale simulations to investigate the dynamic fracture of silica and sodium-silicate glasses under uniaxial tension. The stress-strain curves demonstrate that silica glass is brittle whereas the glasses rich in Na show pronounced ductility. A strong composition dependence is also seen in the crack velocity which is on the order of 1800 m/s for glasses with low Na concentration and decreases to 700 m/s if the concentration is high.

arxiv-2302-13164.title: Multiscale Theory
arxiv-2302-13164.creator: Miroslav Grmela
arxiv-2302-13164.description: Abstract Boltzmann kinetic equation is put into the form of an abstract time evolution equation representing links connecting autonomous mesoscopic dynamical theories involving varying amount of details. In the chronological order we present results that led to the abstract time equation evolution in both state space and the space of vector fields.

arxiv-2304-02546.title: High-energy spin waves in the spin-1 square-lattice antiferromagnet La 2 NiO 4
arxiv-2304-02546.creator: A. N. Petsch, N. S. Headings, D. Prabhakaran, A. I. Kolesnikov, C. D. Frost, A. T. Boothroyd, R. Coldea, S. M. Hayden
arxiv-2304-02546.description: Abstract Inelastic neutron scattering is used to study the magnetic excitations of the S = 1 S=1 square-lattice antiferromagnet La 2 NiO 4 . We find that the spin waves cannot be described by a simple classical (harmonic) Heisenberg model with only nearest-neighbor interactions.

There are many examples of active particles with biological origins, including bacteria and spermatozoa, or with artificial origins, such as self-propelled swimmers and Janus particles. arxiv-2406-02550.title: Learning to grok: Emergence of in-context learning and skill composition in modular arithmetic tasks
arxiv-2406-02550.creator: Tianyu He, Darshil Doshi, Aritra Das, Andrey Gromov
arxiv-2406-02550.description: Abstract Large language models can solve tasks that were not present in the training set. This capability is believed to be due to in-context learning and skill composition. In this work, we study the emergence of in-context learning and skill composition in a collection of modular arithmetic tasks.

arxiv-2407-19384.title: Generation of neutron Airy beams
arxiv-2407-19384.creator: Dusan Sarenac, Owen Lailey, Melissa E. Henderson, Huseyin Ekinci, Charles W. Clark, David G. Cory, Lisa DeBeer-Schmitt, Michael G. Huber, Jonathan S. White, Kirill Zhernenkov, Dmitry A. Pushin
arxiv-2407-19384.description: Abstract The Airy wave packet is a solution to the potential-free Schrödinger equation that exhibits remarkable properties such as self-acceleration, non-diffraction, and self-healing. Although Airy beams are now routinely realized with electromagnetic waves and electrons, the implementation with neutrons has remained elusive due to small transverse coherence lengths, low fluence rates, and the absence of neutron lenses.

arxiv-2502-14174.description: Abstract . We solve a regularized weighted low-rank approximation problem by a stochastic gradient descent on a manifold. pmc-11431515.title: Intranasal Insulin Eases Autism in Rats via GDF-15 and Anti-Inflammatory Pathways
pmc-11431515.creator: Duygu Burcu Arda, Kerem Can Tunç, Mehmet Fatih Bozkurt, Ejder Saylav Bora, Ayşe Çiğel, Oytun Erbaş
pmc-11431515.description: In rat models, it is well-documented that chronic administration of propionic acid (PPA) leads to autism-like behaviors. Although the intranasal (IN) insulin approach is predominantly recognized for its effects on food restriction, it has also been shown to enhance cognitive memory by influencing various proteins, modulating anti-inflammatory pathways in the brain, and reducing signaling molecules such as interleukins.

pmc-11458640.creator: Shan Ding, Fengling Yang, Pan Lai, Weiwen Jiang, Minze Chen, Yijun Ge, Liting Zhou, Shaozhuang Chen, Jiaqi Zhang, Yanrong Ye
pmc-11458640.description: BackgroundThe population of Aging cancer survivors in the United States has surged to over 16.9 million. Research on the relationship between statin usage and post-cancer survival rates remains limited.AimsThis study aims to investigate the association between statin use and various causes of mortality among aging cancer survivors.

pmc-11663972.title: Definition of a framework for volumetric modulated arc therapy plan quality assessment with integration of dose-, complexity-, and robustness metrics
pmc-11663972.creator: Tina Orovwighose, Bernhard Rhein, Oliver Schramm, Oliver Jäkel, Vania Batista
pmc-11663972.description: Highlights•122 metrics were analysed and further reduced via multivariate Spearman analysis.•Prediction of robustness metrics using dose and complexity metrics was introduced.•Metric limits set by statistical process control, with 99 % of metrics within limits.•Based on the amount and strength of correlations, 25 metrics were selected.•Enables early detection of sub-optimal and non-robust radiotherapy plans.

pmc-11708958.title: Pulmonary rehabilitation in connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease: A systematic review
pmc-11708958.creator: Irem Seleoglu, Aynur Demirel
pmc-11708958.description: Background and aim:Interstitial lung disease (ILD) is the major contributor to mortality in between chronic lung diseases. ILD originates from voluminous pathophysiological factors. One of the reasons is connective tissue diseases (CTD). According to experts, patients with CTD-ILD may have a stable disease activity and not need conventional treatment.

pmc-12370046.title: The range and reach of qualitative research in neurosurgery: A scoping review
pmc-12370046.creator: Charlotte J. Whiffin, Kathleen Joy O. Khu, Brandon G. Smith, Isla Kuhn, Santhani M. Selveindran, Laura Hobbs, Samin Davoody, Yusuf Docrat, Orla Mantle, Upamanyu Nath, Lara Onbaşı, Stasa Tumpa, Ignatius N. Esene, Harry Mee, Fergus Gracey, Shobhana Nagraj, Tom Bashford, Angelos G. Kolias, Peter J. Hut
pmc-12370046.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Following calls for more qualitative research in neurosurgery, this scoping review aimed to describe the range and reach of qualitative studies relevant to the field of neurosurgery and the patients and families affected by neurosurgical conditions. A systematic search was conducted in September 2024 across six databases: Medline via Ebsco; Embase via OVID; PsycINFO via Ebsco; Scopus; Web of Science Core Collection; and Global Health via Ebsco. Eligibility criteria were based on Population, Concept, and Context.

pmc-12452564.title: Bacillus Pectinases as Key Biocatalysts for a Circular Bioeconomy: From Green Extraction to Process Optimization and Industrial Scale-Up
pmc-12452564.creator: Fatima Zohra Kaissar, Khelifa Bouacem, Mohammed Lamine Benine, Sondes Mechri, Shubha Rani Sharma, Vishal Kumar Singh, Mahfoud Bakli, Seif El Islam Lebouachera, Giovanni Emiliani, Isabelle Chevalot
pmc-12452564.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Pectins are high-value plant cell-wall polysaccharides with extensive applications in the food, pharmaceutical, textile, paper, and environmental sectors. Traditional extraction and processing methodologies rely heavily on harsh acids, high temperatures, and non-renewable solvents, generating substantial environmental and economic costs. This review consolidates recent advances across the entire Bacillus–pectinase value chain, from green pectin extraction and upstream substrate characterization, through process and statistical optimization of enzyme production, to industrial biocatalysis applications.

pmc-12466578.title: The Effect of Work-Related Use of Information and Communication Technologies on Employees’ Work Goal Progress and Fatigue: Based on the Transactional Model of Stress
pmc-12466578.creator: Xiangping Zhan, Pengfei Zhang, Hongyu Ma, Phillip Ozimek
pmc-12466578.description: The rapid evolution of information and communication technologies (ICTs) has made after-hours work-related ICTs (W_ICTs) use commonplace. The double-edged sword effects of W_ICTs have been widely concerned by researchers, but the role of cognitive appraisal has not been fully investigated.

pmc-12581112.description: Regenerating the missing periodontium represents a difficult task during clinical management of periodontitis given that alveolar bone, periodontal ligament and cementum possess poor regeneration potential. The significant contribution of the inflammatory response to periodontitis occurrence and development has been extensively documented.

pmc-12716107.title: Development of a National Certification Board Reboot and Readiness Course
pmc-12716107.creator: Melicia Escobar, Caitlin Givens, Katie DePalma, Heather M. Bradford
pmc-12716107.description: Pass rates for the American Midwifery Certification Board (AMCB) national certification examination (NCE) are declining. Accreditation Commission for Midwifery Education–accredited midwifery education programs are challenged to meet institutional pass rate goals and support graduates seeking to enter the midwifery workforce. There are financial, emotional, and social consequences for graduates who do not pass the AMCB NCE that undermine their success.

pmc-13232921.title: Gamified Assessment of Cognitive Impulsivity in Eating Disorders and Mental Ill-Health: Mixed Methods Study Incorporating Lived Experience Co-Design and Evaluation
pmc-13232921.creator: Emily Colton, Courtney McLean, Alexandra Anderson, Lauren Hanegraaf, Antonio Verdejo-Garcia
pmc-13232921.description: BackgroundCognitive impulsivity is a multifaceted construct associated with symptom severity, functional impairment, and poor quality of life in eating disorders (EDs) and mental ill-health. uslaw-usc-t22-s5491.title: 22 U.S.C. § 5491 — Suspension of SEED assistance
uslaw-usc-t22-s5491.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t22-s5491.description: United States Code, Title 22 (Foreign Relations And Intercourse); Chapter 63 (Support For East European Democracy (Seed)); Subchapter VII (Miscellaneous Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The President should suspend all assistance to an East European country pursuant to this chapter if the President determines, and reports to the Congress, that— (1) that country is engaged in international activities directly and fundamentally.
